implements a **different output contract than brief.md**, so I used its script only as a parsing cross-check and generated the final files to the brief's spec. The skill's script would have failed the brief on four counts: item format `【hh:mm · 说话人】` instead of the required `【类别 · 相关人】`; 「待定」 instead of 「未明确」/speaker-name fallbacks; a fixed title without the meeting topic; and keyword-priority classification that dropped the 09:39 action item entirely, filed the explicit 履约风险 line under 待办， and left 风险与关注 empty. My classification keeps every entry verbatim-traceable to its transcript line with the attributed speaker (决议 3 / 待办 2 / 风险 2, 合计 7).\n\nVerification: a strict python-docx readback checker (section headers verbatim and ordered, per-item format/numbering/speaker attribution/逐字溯源， table headers and cell sourcing, JSON-vs-docx counts) reports ALL PASS, and the rendered page passed the visual acceptance gate. Note for any follow-up runs: `python-docx` is only in `/usr/bin/python3`, not the default venv `python`.",
